prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Full SCENE STATE SHEET for a physical Mars expedition game. Match the supplied realistic painterly cream-and-teal machinery, ochre landscape, restrained cobalt science equipment, mustard rover fittings. Locally made parts are simple cut straight steel and bolted joints, never elaborate molded industrial machinery. Factory precision parts are imported. No people, text, numerals, labels, captions, borders, arrows, diagrams or UI. Each panel repeats EXACTLY the same camera, framing, object positions, light, room/landscape and perspective, changing ONLY the specified state. Every recurring object is the same actual object. Frame the full installation in the upper two thirds; lower third is quiet natural floor or ground for the movable inventory. No loose decorative objects. Whole scenes will be cropped into registered fixed targets; keep independent working regions clearly separated. Square panels, not portrait strips.
Layout: 3 columns by 1 rows of equal SQUARE scenes. Reading order left to right then next row. Use the FINAL panel of reference 1 as the room and bed structure, preserving its exact left/back/right layout, existing water feed and single shared reservoir. The source is a scene reference, not three separate rooms.
STATE 1: Three medium-filled unplanted zones. The left deep potato bay has a pale translucent liner needing an opaque outer skirt. The rear soybean row is bare medium. The right shallow lettuce shelf has bare medium and an unwicked reservoir edge.
STATE 2: The SAME three beds. A dark opaque foil-backed fabric skirt wraps ONLY the left potato bay sides, with its top still exposed to light. A clean white fabric wick is fitted across the right lettuce tray from its water edge. No plants yet.
STATE 3: The same skirt and wick remain. Small recognizable potato shoots grow in the LEFT bay, young soybean seedlings in the BACK row, little lettuce rosettes in the RIGHT shallow tray. Keep plants confined to their own zones with space between silhouettes.
